skill.description: Operate local Kubernetes clusters with Minikube for development, testing, deployment, and troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Guides local Kubernetes setup, deployment, service access, and debugging with Minikube and kubectl.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static command-execution alerts are Markdown fence false positives, not executable Ruby code. Confirmed risks are limited to explicit shell eval guidance, interactive pod shell access, and a sudo host-file edit, with one added finding for plaintext Kubernetes Secret examples. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden automation.

remediation.issue: Shell eval guidance for Minikube Docker environment
remediation.suggestion: Explain that users should run eval only after confirming they are using a trusted minikube binary and expected PATH.
Require explicit confirmation before sudo host-file changes and offer port-forwarding or manual host mapping as safer alternatives.
Replace literal passwords with clear placeholders and warn users not to commit real secrets or place them in shell history.
Recommend logs, events, describe output, and RBAC checks before using an interactive shell inside a pod.

content.value_statement: Local Kubernetes setup is easy to misconfigure and hard to debug. This skill provides practical Minikube and kubectl workflows for development clusters.
actual_capabilities: Start, stop, delete, and profile Minikube clusters for local development.
Enable common Minikube addons, including ingress, metrics server, dashboard, and storage provisioner.
Build local Docker images for Minikube and apply Kubernetes manifests.
Explain kubectl commands for contexts, namespaces, logs, events, scaling, rollouts, and pod debugging.
Provide example Deployment, Service, ConfigMap, Secret, and Ingress manifests.
Show access options for NodePort, LoadBalancer tunnel, port forwarding, and ingress host mapping.
limitations: It focuses on Minikube and does not cover production Kubernetes operations.
It assumes kubectl, Docker, and Minikube are already installed or can be installed separately.
Some workflows require local shell access and may change cluster or host state.
It provides examples, not environment-specific validation for every cluster configuration.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Local Development Cluster
use_cases.description: Set up Minikube resources, addons, contexts, and image workflow before deploying a service locally.

use_cases.title: Debug a Failing Pod
use_cases.description: Use logs, events, describe output, resource metrics, and container access to isolate local Kubernetes failures.

use_cases.title: Test Kubernetes Manifests Locally
use_cases.description: Create and adjust Deployment, Service, ConfigMap, Secret, and Ingress examples before a cloud deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Minikube Cluster
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me start a local Minikube cluster for a small web application. Include resource settings and essential addons.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a Local Application
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through building local Docker images for Minikube and deploying my Kubernetes manifests from the k8s directory.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Local Kubernetes Networking
prompt_templates.prompt: My service is running in Minikube but I cannot reach it from my browser. Help me compare NodePort, port-forward, tunnel, and ingress options.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Local Cluster Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my local Kubernetes workflow for image loading, namespace context, rollout checks, logs, events, and safe cleanup steps.

output_examples.input: I need a repeatable local cluster setup for a web service.
output: Recommended sequence: start Minikube with enough CPU and memory, then enable ingress and metrics.
Build images inside the Minikube Docker environment, then apply manifests and check rollout status.
Access the service through port forwarding first, then add ingress host mapping when needed.

output_examples.input: My pod keeps restarting after deployment.
output: First check pod events and the previous container logs.
Then verify probes, image names, image pull policy, and resource pressure.
Use an interactive pod shell only when logs and describe output do not provide enough detail.

output_examples.input: I want to test ingress locally before cloud deployment.
output: Enable the Minikube ingress addon and confirm the ingress class name.
Map the local hostname to the Minikube IP after reviewing the host file change.
Validate routing through the service name and target port before testing in a browser.

best_practices: Confirm the active kubectl context and namespace before applying or editing resources.
Use local image tags and explicit image pull policy settings for Minikube-only builds.
Check logs, events, rollout status, and resource usage before opening an interactive pod shell.
anti_patterns: Do not apply manifests to the default context without checking the current cluster.
Do not store real passwords or tokens in sample Secret manifests or shell history.
Do not edit host files with elevated privileges unless the hostname mapping is required and reviewed.

faq.question: Does this skill manage production Kubernetes clusters?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on local Minikube clusters for development and testing.

faq.question: Can it help with kubectl basics?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers contexts, namespaces, logs, events, describe output, scaling, rollouts, and pod debugging.

faq.question: Does it include Kubernetes manifest examples?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, Secrets, and Ingress resources.

faq.question: Can it help use local Docker images in Minikube?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to build images for Minikube and use local image pull settings.

faq.question: Does it require privileged host changes?
faq.answer: Only some ingress hostname workflows require host file edits. Review those steps before running them.

faq.question: Is it compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
